description: We are the team NOVA METRICS - VI from Hamdard University Bangladesh.
summary:
Earth Metamorphosis is an AI-powered disaster monitoring platform developed for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge. Utilizing NASA-ISRO's NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, our system detects surface changes such as floods, landslides, and river erosion, even through heavy cloud cover where optical satellites fail.

The platform features an interactive 3D Cesium Globe where users can draw a custom Area of Interest (AOI). The backend then queries NASA's Earthdata CMR API to find real NISAR granules, automatically downloads the HDF5 files, and runs a D-SAR-D pipeline (change detection using HH and HV polarization). It then generates a transparent red flood mask and real-time statistics (coverage %, affected area in km²).

By transforming complex satellite data into visual, actionable insights, Earth Metamorphosis addresses critical disaster management needs in Bangladesh, a riverine country highly vulnerable to monsoon flooding.
details:
What it does:
Earth Metamorphosis is a full-stack web application that visualizes surface changes using real NISAR SAR data. Users can select preset locations (like Feni) or draw a custom bounding box on a 3D globe. The system fetches the optimal "Before" and "After" NISAR granules, processes the backscatter data, and overlays a red flood mask on the globe.

How it works (Technical):

  • Frontend: Next.js 15 (TypeScript) with CesiumJS for 3D globe rendering, Zustand for state management, and Recharts for data visualization.
  • Backend: Python FastAPI, using earthaccess and direct NASA CMR API calls for data retrieval, rasterio/h5py for HDF5 processing, and numpy for change detection math.
  • Data Flow: The backend calculates the difference in HH and HV backscatter. A pixel is flagged as flooded if both polarizations drop below a specific threshold. We then generate a GeoTIFF, a 2-panel preview image, and a transparent red overlay, which we Base64-encode and send directly to the frontend to avoid storage issues.

Impact:
Optical satellites are blind during monsoon clouds. NISAR's L-band SAR penetrates clouds and works at night, providing life-saving, rapid disaster intelligence for flood-prone regions like Bangladesh.

Creative factors:
We designed a fully interactive 3D globe experience instead of static maps. We also implemented an "Auto-pick" algorithm that intelligently selects the best matching satellite pairs (same track/frame) to ensure accurate change detection.
